format_instruction: Return only raw Python source or exactly one Python or untyped fenced code block. Include the required function definition and any imports it needs. Do not include prose or multiple code blocks. Use the Python standard library only. Returned values are compared using Python equality; numeric type identity, resource efficiency and behavior outside the stated input domain are not scored.

tasks.prompt: Return the binomial coefficient n choose r, reduced modulo p, as an integer in the range from 0 through p-1. Inputs n, r and p are integers with 0 <= r <= n and p >= 1. The modulus need not be prime.

boundary_cases.reason: DEFECT FIX: a prime-only Lucas implementation returns 0; v1's only composite-modulus case (6,3,4) coincides with Lucas, so the suite did not test the public 'modulus need not be prime' claim
second composite-modulus case on which prime-only Lucas returns 0
p = 1 with r >= 1: regression guard for the modulus-one path beyond r = 0

negative_controls.rationale: Constant zero fails cases with a nonzero remainder.

reference_repair.label: mbpp/402 reference-repair-v1
reference_repair.change: append ' % p' to the return expression: `return C[r]` -> `return C[r] % p`; CRLF and trailing whitespace preserved
reference_repair.static_proof_summary: C[0] is set to 1 and never rewritten (the inner range stops before j = 0), so r = 0 returned an unreduced 1 -- wrong only when p = 1; the added % p makes it 0. For j >= 1 every write is reduced mod p, so C[r] already lies in [0, p-1] and the extra % p is a no-op; for r = 0 and p >= 2, 1 % p = 1. Pascal's recurrence holds modulo any m >= 1, so primality is not required. The repair therefore changes exactly the p = 1, r = 0 outputs and nothing else in-domain.
reference_repair.adversarial_verdict: REPAIR_HOLDS -- no counterexample across p = 1 (r = 0 and r >= 1), composite p, r = n, n = 0, and the original three assertions
reference_repair.status: proposed; not adopted until isolated execution of original vs repaired passes a committed validation contract

tasks.prompt: Return the number of occurrences of the largest integer in arr. arr is a nonempty list of integers, which can be negative, zero or positive; n is an integer equal to len(arr). Return the count as an integer.

boundary_cases.reason: the count-arr[0] control returns 1; in all three v1 boundary cases arr[0] is the maximum, so only the original assertions caught it

negative_controls.rationale: Returns the maximum value rather than its frequency.
Counts the first value even when it is not the maximum.

tasks.prompt: Return the arithmetic mean of all positive odd integers from 1 through n, including n. n is a positive odd integer. This mean is an integer; return that exact integer value. Behavior for even, zero or negative n is outside this task contract.

negative_controls.rationale: Returns the last value rather than the mean.
Rounds half of n down, one below the required mean.
